# A spread written as a slot insertion's or an event's argument reaches the
# interpreter as an ir.Spread, not only as a list element.
#
# The checker expands `...x` in a call's argument list into named arguments,
# but a slot insertion and an emit check the raw argument, so the Spread
# survives into SlotInst.Args and Emit.Args. The interpreter's Eval has to
# evaluate one to its operand; without that arm both tests below panic with
# "testrunner.Eval: unhandled ir.Expr *ir.Spread" before any assertion runs.

sngl test --platform none spread.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

-- spread.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

struct Row {
    title string = ""
}

component table(r Row, cell component(Row)) node {
    vbox {
        cell(...r)
    }
}

component slotted node {
    var seen = ""
    table(r=Row{title="hello"}) {
        component cell(row) {
            text(value=row.title)
        }
    }
    button #go(text="go", @click { seen = "clicked" })
}

func testSpreadIntoSlot(t Test, c slotted) {
    c.go.click()
    t.assert(c.seen == "clicked")
}

component emitter(@fired ChangeEvent) node {
    var ev = ChangeEvent{value="v"}
    button #go(text="go", @click { fired(...ev) })
}

component listener node {
    var got = ""
    emitter #e(@fired(x) { got = x.value })
}

func testSpreadIntoEmit(t Test, c listener) {
    c.e.go.click()
    t.assert(c.got == "v")
}
